articles.title: When Workers, Driving Customers or Saving Lives in the ER, Become Independent Contractors
articles.author: Boston DSA
articles.content_excerpt: [[{“value”:” By: Matt Wolfinger BOSTON – There’s a loophole in our labor laws spreading across the economy. From delivery drivers to nurses, corporations are classifying workers as independent contractors and using the promise of flexible work to cudgel labor rights. Nearly 12 million people in the United States, or seven percent of the workforce, describe independent contractor work as their primary source of income, according to the most recent data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Independent contractors aren’t protected under the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA), so they can’t unionize, aren’t entitled to benefits, a minimum wage, or overtime and can be fired at will. articles.title: Turkey Risks Being Drawn Into Saudi Arabia’s War in Yemen
articles.author: Oğul Tuna
articles.content_excerpt: There are few places outside Turkey that occupy such a mournful place in the country’s popular memory as Yemen. For generations, Turks who knew little about the politics of the Arabian Peninsula nevertheless knew Yemen through folk songs. They were ballads about young men sent from Anatolia to fight in Yemen, many of whom never returned. They told of mothers waiting for sons, women waiting for husbands, and a distant land associated above all with death. One of the most haunting was recorded by Ruhi Su, the great communist interpreter of Turkish folk music. Its refrain addresses the country with a bitter grandeur: Yemen, Yemen, glorious Yemen, Yemen, Yemen, your soil soaked in blood. The glory belonged to the empire. articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Financial institutions manage client relationships through onboarding, verification, account servicing, reviews, and closure. Each stage creates tasks, decisions, records, and compliance obligations that require consistent handling. When teams manage these activities separately, information becomes fragmented, and delays increase. That is where a structured, end-to-end process adds the most value. Client lifecycle management connects the full relationship into one structured process, giving teams clearer ownership, better data, and stronger oversight. articles.title: How Israel Controls Palestinian Land
articles.author: Vijay Prashad
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Israel’s genocidal bombing campaign has devastated Gaza’s wastewater system, destroying or damaging nearly 90% of the territory’s water and sanitation infrastructure since 2023. Every day, 45,000 cubic metres of untreated sewage are discharged into the Mediterranean Sea while an additional 15,000 cubic metres seep into the ground. This collapse of sanitation infrastructure has led to an infestation of rats and other rodents in Gaza, with two in three children living in displacement sites plagued by these vermin. articles.author: Sonali Kolhatkar
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Journalism is experiencing one of its worst crises when it’s needed the most. Overall, news consumption is dropping . And it’s worse among young people , who largely get their news through social media, not news outlets. People under 30, more than any other age group, trust social media sources of news. The problem is that it’s hard to tell if your favorite social media source is a citizen journalist or a paid promoter. In a recent in-depth report , The New York Times revealed that social media platforms are rife with accounts that are paid to promote campaigns parading as personal opinion. articles.title: Trump Is Steering
articles.author: Tom Engelhardt
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Here’s the truth of it: after all these years, today I don’t know what to write about. I mean, in this ever-stranger world of ours, where even to start? Oh, wait, give me a second and I’ll be right back! I don’t want to miss the latest ads featuring our president , paid for with millions of our tax dollars. It’s obviously important to check them out since, as he told us recently, “I’m not promoting myself because I’m not running for office. I’m promoting the country.” And who wouldn’t want him to reassure us about the state of this fair land of ours? As he put it in one of those ads, “America will never be a communist country.” Whew! Who among us wasn’t worried about that!

articles.title: Climate Policies Can Bring Relief on Affordability and Beyond
articles.author: Rithika Ramamurthy
articles.content_excerpt: As the US midterm elections approach, one word keeps coming up in campaign promises and headlines: “ affordability .” That working people in the United States are struggling to afford basic necessities is a problem that many are willing to acknowledge, but there is very little agreement on what should be done to tackle a core driver of the affordability crisis: climate change. The climate crisis is already making life more expensive . Electricity rates skyrocketed in 2025 due to historic heat waves; home insurance rates are rising as disasters and extreme weather patterns increase; transportation costs have become one of the biggest sources of financial burden because of the volatile price of fossil fuels. articles.title: Historian Eric Hobsbawm Was a “Communist Polymath”
articles.author: Emile Chabal
articles.content_excerpt: Eric Hobsbawm’s life began just as the “long nineteenth century” was drawing to a close. Born in Alexandria, Egypt, and formed as a youth in Red Vienna and Weimar-era Berlin, he came to intellectual maturity in interwar Cambridge and postwar London. articles.title: How Bernie’s Campaigns Reorganized the Organized Left
articles.author: Hadas Thier
articles.content_excerpt: Ten years ago, while socialist Bernie Sanders was making his historic run for the Democratic presidential nomination that drew millions of supporters and promised a “political revolution” to live long past his campaign, I was part of a small revolutionary organization that pooh-poohed him as a faux renegade. The socialist left at the time had been largely marginal to the American political landscape. This was not only because so few socialists sat in political offices. articles.title: Proles: A Story of Post-Sixties’ Salting Among the “Salt of The Earth”
articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: In the early 1970s, when many student activists were migrating from campus to industrial jobs to promote working class radicalization, no labor film was more influential than Salt of the Earth. This pioneering docudrama was made two decades earlier by a producer, writer, director, and several actors who were unemployable in Hollywood, due to McCarthy era-blacklisting. This left-wing creative team recruited a cast of workers and their families from the International Union of Mine, Mill, and Smelter Workers (IUMMSW) to play themselves in a fictional account of a long strike at the Empire Zinc Company in Grant County, New Mexico. articles.title: The Margin of Effort: How Election Volunteering Can Help Save Democracy
articles.author: Paul Rogat Loeb
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Sometimes it’s the humble actions that matter, an important lesson for our dangerous time. For years, I’ve volunteered to get out the vote for my preferred candidates. In one election, knocking on doors in a Seattle neighborhood, I spoke with three people who supported my candidate for governor but wouldn’t have voted had I not contacted them: One forgot it was Election Day. Another didn’t know how to submit an absentee ballot. The third needed a ride to the polls. My impact had nothing to do with eloquence or skill and everything to do with simply showing up. articles.title: Britain’s Military-Industrial Complex Is Promoting War Fever
articles.author: John Rees
articles.content_excerpt: War fever has gripped the European political establishment. War in Ukraine and rumors of continent-wide conflict with Russia are now the staple justification for rearmament, ballooning arms budgets, and the reintroduction of conscription across Europe. Popular consent for this lurch to militarization is very limited indeed, so the political establishment is deploying military and security service officers, past and present, in an unprecedented propaganda blitz to make the case for war. Astounding statistics underline how far this process has gone. In the last twelve months, there have been approximately nine hundred appearances by serving or former military or security service officers on Britain’s mainstream media.
